newsitem.title: SPAIN: TENNIS-COSTA BRUSHES ASIDE PORTAS TO WIN BARCELONA OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-COSTA BRUSHES ASIDE PORTAS TO WIN BARCELONA OPEN.

text.p: Albert Costa brushed aside fellow Spaniard Albert Portas to win the Barcelona Open on Monday, the day he moved into the top 10 of the world rankings for the first time.
Costa never looked in trouble during his 7-5 6-4 6-4 victory over Portas, a qualifier who was playing the first best-of-five-set match of his life.
"Getting to the top 10 is nice, but winning the Barcelona Open is much nicer," said Costa.
The final had been moved to Monday because of heavy rain in Barcelona on Sunday.
Portas, returning from a recent six-month lay-off due to a knee injury, was made to look out of his depth by Costa, who broke once in each set without losing his own serve.
Portas, who started the tournament world ranked 133, was let down by his powerful forehand which had helped him to victory in earlier rounds over seeded players Marcelo Rios and Alberto Berasategui.
The match had gone with serve until the 11th game of the first set when Portas committed three errors to lose the game to love.
Costa took the set in the next game, and broke again in the fifth game of the second set, before coasting to victory over the only qualifier ever to reach the final of the Barcelona tournament.
"I was rather nervous in the first set, but I won the points at the key moments," said Costa. "After the break in the second set I saw victory much closer."
